interface.title: LitePhospho — Explainable Phosphosite Predictor
interface.field: Proteomics / bioinformatics (predicting where proteins are phosphorylated)
interface.stage_of_work: Hypothesis generation and prioritisation before experiments (in-silico screening of candidate sites)
interface.what_it_is_for: Paste a human protein sequence and get a phosphorylation probability for every S/T/Y residue, with predicted sites highlighted on the sequence at an adjustable decision threshold. Then pick one site and see which neighbouring residues in a ±15-residue window drove its score, using an occlusion (deletion) test.

data.note: The built-in p53 N-terminal fragment (60 aa, MEEPQSDPSVEPPLSQETFSDLWKLLPENNVLSPLPSQAMDDLMLSPDDIEQWFTEDPGP) came from 'Load example (p53)'. I also pasted four sequences: a p53 S15A variant (once with a FASTA header and once without), a sequence with no S/T/Y, a 97-aa coronavirus N-protein-like fragment (length per screens/020.webp), and a junk string with non-standard letters, digits and '*'. The app has no file upload.

tree.general: Predict which residues of a protein are likely modified, and see which neighbouring positions drive each call, so you can judge how far to trust it
tree.specific: Predict S/T/Y phosphosites in a pasted protein sequence, inspect them at a chosen threshold, and explain individual sites with the occlusion importance window

features.name: Threshold-linked inline sequence highlighter with per-residue score tooltips
features.general: Show a long string of items with every item above a user-chosen score cutoff highlighted, show a live count of positives, and reveal each candidate's exact score on hover, so moving the cutoff instantly changes the calls without recomputing
features.specific: Show the protein sequence in monospace with predicted S/T/Y phosphosites (probability ≥ Decision threshold) shaded green. Hovering any S/T/Y shows 'pos N: p' as a native title tooltip. The 'Predicted phosphosites (≥t)' count and the highlights follow the sidebar slider
steps: Run the prediction so every candidate residue has a probability
Read the highlighted residues and the predicted-count summary at the default 0.50
Hover a residue to see its position and probability
Drag the Decision threshold slider (or use the arrow keys, step 0.05) to make the call stricter or looser
Watch the highlights and the count update, after a brief rerun, without predicting again
serves_tasks: Make the cutoff stricter or looser and see the calls update
Read the score for each individual candidate
Score every candidate position and see the summary counts

features.name: Paste-sequence input with example loader, cleaning and summary metrics
features.general: Take a pasted sequence (or a built-in reference example), normalise it, run a model on it, and report summary counts, warning when the input is empty or has nothing to score
features.specific: The text area takes one-letter amino acids. 'Load example (p53)' fills it with the p53 fragment. 'Predict phosphosites' uppercases the text and drops digits, spaces and symbols. Non-standard letters (B/J/O/U/X/Z) stay in the displayed sequence and the length tile, but are not scored. The app then reports Sequence length, S/T/Y candidate sites and Predicted phosphosites
steps: Press Load example (p53), or paste your own sequence without a FASTA header
Commit the text (Ctrl+Enter, or the first click on Predict)
Read the three metric tiles, or the warning when the box is empty or has no S/T/Y
Paste a variant or a new protein and predict again to compare
serves_tasks: Score every candidate position and see the summary counts
Score a point-mutant variant and compare with the reference
See how the tool handles inputs with nothing to score or with invalid characters
